items: Acetylcholine acts between motor neurons and skeletal muscle fibres, and between many neurons.
Biogenic amines are excitatory neurotransmitters. They also function as hormones. These include;
Norepinephrine is made in CNS and sympathetic nerves. It regulates sleep patterns, focus and alertness.
Epinephrine is released in adrenal glands and the brainstem. It plays a role in sleep. It also enables to become and stay alert.
Dopamine is a neurotransmitter in brain. It controls body movements, pleasures related to motivation and also emotional stimulation.
Serotonin is produced by the neurons in intestine (approximately 90%), and CNS (10%). It regulates appetite, sleep, memory and learning, temperature, mood, behaviour, muscle contraction etc.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text:
Degeneration of dopamine-releasing neurons produces the muscle tremors of Parkinson’s disease.
Insufficient activity of serotonin-releasing neurons may cause depression. Many antidepressant drugs block the elimination of serotonin from the synaptic cleft. So, serotonin remains in the synaptic cleft and reduces depression.

These neurotransmitters decrease the chance of transmission of nerve impulse to the postsynaptic neuron. When they bind to the receptors on postsynaptic neuron, channels for chloride ions open instead of opening sodium channels (which would excite the cell). As a result, chloride ions diffuse into neuron and make the inside of the membrane even more negative than RPM. This hyperpolarization causes inhibitory effect. blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: “RPM” is a misprint for RMP (resting membrane potential): chloride ions make the inside of the membrane even more negative than the resting membrane potential.

items: Gamma - aminobutyric acid (GABA) is the chief inhibitory neurotransmitter in CNS. It reduces the neural excitability throughout the nervous system. It helps to control and regulate various physiological and behavioural processes. It reduces anxiety, stress, and fear, and promotes relaxation and sleep.
Glycine is an inhibitory neurotransmitter especially in the spinal cord, brainstem, and retina.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: Many sedative drugs enhance the binding of GABA to its receptors and so increase the effectiveness of GABA at the synapse.

Endorphins are inhibitory neurotransmitters released by neurons in brain. They reduce the release of excitatory neurotransmitters responsible for transmitting pain messages. In this way, they block the pain signals to reach the concerned part of the brain.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: Opium and its derivatives, morphine and heroin, have an analgesic (pain-reducing) effect because they are similar in chemical structure to endorphins. So, they easily bind to the receptors of endorphins.

blocks.title: Effect of nerve gas on neurotransmitter acetylcholine
blocks.text: The excitatory neurotransmitter acetylcholine is released by motor neurons at neuromuscular junctions. It stimulates the skeletal muscles to contract. Then, it is broken down by acetylcholinesterase enzyme. A nerve gas (e.g., sarin, tabun, soman) is a highly toxic chemical that inhibits this enzyme. This inhibition leads to the accumulation of acetylcholine, causing overstimulation of skeletal muscle and cause muscles to remain contracted. If the diaphragm muscle remains contracted, the person is not be able to breathe. Other effects may include muscle twitching, convulsions, respiratory distress, and ultimately death.
